# First Level Header

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.  To get quick help, one might use *Help* -> *Markdown Quick Reference*.

## Second Level Header

When you click the ***Render*** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

### Third Level Header

Consider using data (Data Frame) from an `R` package such as `PASWR2`.  First the package must be loaded (if it is installed - `PASWR2` is installed on the server) using the function `library()`.

```{r}
#| message: false
# Using message: false will remove messages that may appear after running certain functions.
library(PASWR2)
# show the first five rows of VIT2005
head(VIT2005)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
ggplot(data = VIT2005, aes(x = area, y = totalprice)) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_currency(prefix = "€"))
ggplot(data = VIT2005, aes(x = area, y = totalprice, color = as.factor(elevator))) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_currency(
    big.mark = ".", 
      decimal.mark = ",", 
      suffix = "€", 
      prefix = "")
    ) 

ggplot(data = VIT2005, aes(x = area, y = totalprice, color = as.factor(elevator))) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_currency(
    big.mark = ".", 
      decimal.mark = ",", 
      suffix = "€", 
      prefix = "")
    ) +
  labs(color = "Elevator")
```

### Some Descriptive statistics

```{r}
VIT2005$elevator <- factor(VIT2005$elevator, levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
VIT2005 |> 
  group_by(elevator) |> 
  summarize(Mean_Area = mean(area), MeanTotalprice = mean(totalprice))
ggplot(data = VIT2005, aes(x = area, y = totalprice, color = elevator)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_currency(
    big.mark = ".", 
      decimal.mark = ",", 
      suffix = "€", 
      prefix = "")
    ) +
  labs(color = "Elevator")
```

Let's make the output look better:

```{r}
VIT2005 |> 
  group_by(elevator) |> 
  summarize(Mean_Area = mean(area), Mean_TotalPrice = mean(totalprice)) -> stuff
library(knitr)
kable(stuff)
```

Use some inline `r` code now to report the average area for apartments with elevators.

The average area for apartments with an elevator is `r round(stuff$Mean_Area[2],2)` $\text{m}^2$.


## Boxplot(s)

```{r}
ggplot(data = VIT2005, aes(y = totalprice)) + 
  geom_boxplot()
ggplot(data = VIT2005, aes(y = totalprice, x = elevator, fill = elevator)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw()
```
